principles: Feature work dominates. Foundational work earns its place by unblocking the feature in focus, and says which one in its goal.
One focus at a time. A feature is not done when it compiles, it is done when it is playtestable and has an audit report the user can act on.

The user's mocks are the design floor. They are ideas to build on, which means a runner may go further than a mock, never below it or away from it: its look, layout, controls, copy length and interactions are what ships. A departure is a decision card, never a quiet rewrite, and a mock page is never edited to match the code.
Delight and ease are acceptance criteria, not aspirations. If a feature works but feels clumsy, it is not done.
Only epics staged now may hold open tasks. Anything serving a later epic waits, so we ship something finished instead of everything half-built.

Ask the grown-up-tool question every time: would someone who knows Premiere (for video) or Photoshop (for pictures) find this where they expect it, and is it easier here? Actions live where you click: a right-click menu on the thing, not a tool or a panel button for everything.
A feature exists only if a person running Next with default settings can reach it. A walk that forces a flag proves nothing about what the user sees.

children.title: Better than Premiere at editing screen recordings
children.note: Standing objective from the user (2026-09-23: "better than premiere"). Measured against Premiere Pro, Final Cut, ScreenFlow and Screen Studio on one workflow: a five minute talking screen recording cut to ninety seconds with a second clip, a music bed, a transition, a title, captions and an MP4. The gap report is docs/design/video-vs-premiere.md; re-run the session and update it whenever a gap closes. The manager files against the criteria below.
success: Every Premiere key on the gap report does its Premiere job on a video document straight after it opens, with no click first: J K L, I O, M, B, V, Q W, apostrophe and semicolon, = - and backslash, S, Command K, Shift Delete, and a default transition key
The five minute workflow takes no more presses than Premiere: removing a marked stretch is at most three presses (I, O, one key), and the whole cut to ninety seconds is under 40 presses and drags
On a five minute recording with its captions written, no press on the timeline and no frame of playback keeps the main thread busy over 50 ms
Captions for five minutes of speech write themselves in under 10 seconds on this Mac (measured 2026-09-24: about 3 s, already ahead of Premiere)
The ruler, playhead, clips and captions agree to the frame at every zoom, and a title, the export size and the export sheet need no restyling or guessing to come out right for sharing at 1080p
